newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans to lift Islamic headscarf ban.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans to lift Islamic headscarf ban.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-led government is planning to lift a ban on female civil servants and students wearing the Islamic headscarf in workplaces and universities, an aide to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Monday.
"There is a change being planned in the rule on civil servants' dress code. This will be approved by the cabinet," Welfare Party MP Oguzhan Asilturk told Reuters.

At the moment, strictly secularist Turkey can discipline its female civil servants for wearing the headscarf and sack them for repeated offences. University rectors can forbid the headscarf at their discretion.
Asilturk said the wording of the planned changes would probably be wide enough for the headscarf to be worn anywhere.
"Women civil servants who want to cover their heads will be able to do so," he said.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, has mostly steered clear of introducing Islamic norms into public life since he came to power in coalition last June.
